cards.back: ~3400 BCE — Sumer (Mesopotamia). Cuneiform script on clay tablets. Enabled record-keeping and literature.

cards.front: Construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza
cards.back: ~2560 BCE — Egypt. Built for Pharaoh Khufu. Tallest man-made structure for 3,800 years.
509 BCE — Rome. Overthrow of the last king, Tarquinius Superbus. Established the Senate and consuls.
~461–429 BCE — Greece. Under Pericles. Flourishing of democracy, philosophy, drama, and the Parthenon.
336–323 BCE — Macedon/Greece. Conquered Persia, Egypt, and parts of India. Spread Hellenistic culture.
27 BCE — Rome. Augustus became first emperor after civil wars. Beginning of the Roman Empire.

cards.front: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
cards.back: 476 CE — Romulus Augustulus deposed by Odoacer. Marks the traditional end of ancient history in the West.
622 CE — Prophet Muhammad's migration (Hijra) to Medina. Foundation of the Islamic calendar and community.
800 CE — Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne. United much of Western Europe; the "Father of Europe."
1066 — William the Conqueror defeated Harold II at the Battle of Hastings. Reshaped English culture and language.
1215 — England. King John forced to sign. Limited royal power; foundation for constitutional law.
1347–1351 — Bubonic plague killed ~30–60% of Europe's population. Transformed social and economic structures.
1453 — Ottoman Turks captured the Byzantine capital. End of the Eastern Roman Empire. Shift in trade routes.
~1440 — Germany. Johannes Gutenberg's movable-type press. Revolutionized information spread and literacy.
1492 — Sponsored by Spain. Landed in the Bahamas. Began the era of European exploration and colonization.
1517 — Martin Luther's 95 Theses. Challenged Catholic Church practices. Led to Protestantism and religious wars.

cards.front: Spanish Conquest of the Aztec Empire
cards.back: 1519–1521 — Hernán Cortés conquered Tenochtitlan. Fall of the Aztec Empire; beginning of Spanish colonial Mexico.
~1543–1687 — Copernicus, Galileo, Newton. Shift from religious to empirical understanding of nature.
1642–1651 — Parliamentarians vs. Royalists. King Charles I executed (1649). Temporary republic under Cromwell.
July 4, 1776 — Thirteen colonies declared independence from Britain. Written primarily by Thomas Jefferson.
1789–1799 — Overthrow of the monarchy. Storming of the Bastille (July 14, 1789). Rise of Napoleon followed.
1791–1804 — Enslaved people in Saint-Domingue overthrew French colonial rule. First successful slave revolt; Haiti independent 1804.
1803–1815 — Napoleon Bonaparte's campaigns across Europe. Ended at Waterloo. Redrew European borders.

cards.front: Abolition of Slavery in the British Empire
cards.back: 1833 — Slavery Abolition Act. Freed ~800,000 enslaved people across British colonies (effective 1834).
1848 — Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels. Outlined class struggle and called for workers' revolution.
1861–1865 — Union (North) vs. Confederacy (South). ~620,000 dead. Ended slavery (13th Amendment).
1868 — Japan. Ended the Tokugawa shogunate. Rapid modernization and industrialization under Emperor Meiji.
1914–1918 — Allied Powers vs. Central Powers. ~17 million dead. Redrew map of Europe; League of Nations formed.
1917 — Bolsheviks overthrew the Tsar. Led by Lenin. Established the Soviet Union (1922).
1920 — 19th Amendment ratified. Granted American women the right to vote.
1929–1939 — Triggered by the Wall Street Crash (Oct 1929). Global economic devastation and mass unemployment.
1939–1945 — Allies vs. Axis powers. ~70–85 million dead. Holocaust. Atomic bombs on Japan. UN founded.
August 15, 1947 — India gained independence from Britain. Partition created India and Pakistan.
1945 — 51 nations signed the UN Charter in San Francisco. Goal: prevent future world wars.
1949 — Mao Zedong's Communist Party defeated the Nationalists. Established the People's Republic of China.
1954–1968 — Led by Martin Luther King Jr. and others. Desegregation, Civil Rights Act (1964), Voting Rights Act (1965).
July 20, 1969 — Apollo 11. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin. "One small step for man..."
November 9, 1989 — Symbolized end of the Cold War. Led to German reunification (1990).
December 26, 1991 — End of the Cold War. 15 independent republics. Russia emerged as successor state.
September 11, 2001 — Al-Qaeda attacked the US. ~3,000 killed. Led to the War on Terror.
